brief: JPM's morning briefing frames September CPI (Feroli: headline +0.55% m/m, 3.6% y/y; core +0.18% m/m, 2.4% y/y) as consistent with the Fed skipping October and hiking in December; a core print near 0.18% would push global yields lower and support rate-sensitive baskets. ASML's margin-led Q3 beat and raised FY26 sales guide lifted the stock 1.3% but did not restart the broader Semiconductor/Memory trade (Micron fell pre-market) after SOX's five-session losing streak; JPM's Scott Silver contrasts this quarter's low-single-digit estimate revisions with the prior quarter's ~30% cut that still saw the stock fall. Day-1 bank earnings (card spending +10% at JPM, +13% at Citi; falling delinquencies at Citi/Wells Fargo) read through to a resilient-consumer thesis JPM reflags using Chase data showing September spending growth accelerating to 6.6% y/y across income cohorts, even as the JPM Retail basket sits 8.7% below its August peak with light long/short positioning. JPM's Rob O'Dwyer argues bank weakness reflects quant/passive flow, not fundamentals, and is a buying opportunity. JPM reiterates its Tactically Bullish equity view into earnings, preferring Tech and Cyclicals.

cards.claim: JPM economist Michael Feroli forecasts September headline CPI at 0.55% month-over-month (3.6% year-over-year) and core CPI at 0.18% month-over-month (2.4% year-over-year).
cards.anchor: Feroli sees Headline MoM of 0.55% (3.6% YoY) and Core MoM of 0.18% (2.4% YoY)
cards.topic: CPI inflation surprise and Fed pricing

cards.claim: JPM expects a CPI print in line with its forecast to keep the bond market from pricing in an October rate hike, with a skip in October and a December hike remaining most likely.
cards.anchor: keep the bond market from re-pricing an October hike, instead continuing to see a skip and a December hike as most likely
cards.topic: CPI inflation surprise and Fed pricing

cards.claim: JPM expects global bond yields to move lower and rate-sensitive baskets to be supported if core CPI comes in around 0.18% month-over-month.
cards.anchor: If core MoM comes in around 0.18%, we'd expect yields to move lower globally, which tends to support rate-sensitive baskets
cards.topic: CPI inflation surprise and Fed pricing

cards.claim: JPM notes the market is currently pricing a December Fed hike followed by two more hikes in fiscal year 2027, and that dovish inflation prints removing hike expectations would push bond yields lower.
cards.anchor: dovish inflation prints could remove further hike expectations out of the market which is currently pricing a Dec hike and then 2x hikes in FY27
cards.topic: CPI inflation surprise and Fed pricing
